newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco signs $1 bln deal with Lyonnaise des Eaux.
newsitem.headline: Morocco signs $1 bln deal with Lyonnaise des Eaux.

text.p: Morocco on Monday signed a 9.6 billion dirham ($1 billion) deal with the French firm Lyonnaise des Eaux to take over the management of Casablanca's water and electricity distribution.
At a ceremony presided over by Moroccan Interior Minister Driss Basri and Lyonnaise des Eaux chairman Jerome Monod, the two parties signed the long-awaited accord.

"The contract we finalised today with Lyonnaise des Eaux is a part of the government programme aimed at transferring public services to the private sector to improve its management and development," Basri told the meeting.

Casablanca, Morocco's financial centre, negotiated with Lyonnaise des Eaux for nearly two years. The French firm takes over the running of the city's water, electricity and public waste systems for 30 years from the second quarter of 1997.

The firm plans an investment of 9.6 billion dirhams out of a total of 30 billion dirhams investment over 30 years. The city's four million consumers and other parties are expected to provide the rest of the investment, an official said.

Basri said a private company with a capital of 800 million dirhams would be set up. The main shareholders would be Lyonnaise des Eaux and its subsidiaries. The other members were identified as Spanish Endesar and Agua de Barcelona.
The minister said the French firm planned the extension of water and electricity services to 40,000 Casablanca inhabitants every five years.

Earlier, the Moroccan CGEM confederation of businessmen argued over the deal and said the French firm would invest only two billion dirhams in equipment which would remain its property, while more than seven billion dirhams to its charge would come from the urban community.
The confederation said water, electricity and waste charges would rise.

"The French firm has pledged not to increase water and electricity charges in the next 12 months. A moderate increase in those services will be observed in the second and third year of the contract and from the second year for waste charges," Casablanca municipal official Abdelmoughet Slimani said.
The deal between the urban community and the French firm was approved last April 15.
